answer.rationale: The binding constraint this cycle is delivery risk, not price: the line is at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer and the contract lapses in 14 days. That rules out switch_primary_vendor — memory_c2 records real unit-cost savings from the low-cost vendor but also an explicit caveat (SLA missed in three of four quarters; not to be sole source on a critical line), and a migration under a 14-day cliff with no buffer is exactly the scenario the caveat warns against. defer_decision (memory_c5) worked only for a non-critical service on month-to-month terms; this contract does not auto-renew, so deferring means an uncovered primary line. add_second_source (memory_c3) is the right structural fix for concentration risk but consumes the single decision without touching the 18% mandate, and it cannot stand up new allocation inside 14 days. That leaves renewal-side action, and negotiate_terms dominates plain renew_incumbent: memory_c1 says renewal preserves integration stability, while memory_c4 says benchmarked renegotiation at renewal recovered real margin on both price and payment terms — so negotiating captures the c1 stability benefit plus cost movement. I want the c4 source record to see whether the recovered margin was anywhere near 18% or merely a few points, and the c6 record to check whether the multi-year volume discount is a legitimate additional lever here or was conditioned on circumstances that no longer hold (a multi-year lock also cuts against later dual-sourcing, so its terms matter). Risk I am flagging downstream: the 18% mandate creates pressure to convert a cost target into a sole-source move on the cheap vendor, which would trade a measurable saving for an unmeasured stockout exposure on a line with no buffer. If verification shows negotiation plus volume terms cannot plausibly reach 18%, the honest output is a partial saving now plus a flagged gap and a queued second-source action next review — not a reliability trade to make the number. I am also treating these as consolidated summaries whose original context may be narrower than the one-line claim suggests.
